title: Closet eval scratchpad: micro-regression triage
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal triage notes after noticing an uptick in short/abrupt answers post rollout (v2.1.7 -> v2.2.0). This is a scratchpad: hypotheses, tiny rubric for spot checks, a few raw samples, sampling plan, and immediate next steps. Not polished — notes to self and Ivy/Noah for pair debugging.

Observations (what triggered this):
- Production latency and token-cost looked fine, but manual sampling during smoke tests showed more truncated completions and odd ellipsis-like endings.
- Increase in short answers predominantly on prompts with explicit instruction lists or bullet-style context.
- Occurs across models in the rollout group (model-A-q4/8-bit and model-A-q4/16-bit), more frequent on the 8-bit variant.

Quick hypothesis list (ranked):
1) Batching/windowing change in serving runtime causes earlier stop_token detection when prefix contains list markers ("-", "1.").
2) New kernel selection introduced a micro-change in generation loop that favors stop probability after punctuation.
3) Quantization+temperature interaction: 8-bit quantization amplifies top-k filtering artifacts for certain tokens.
4) Hidden: a tokenizer update (merge ops) dropped a rare token making the model more likely to predict EOS.

Ad-hoc micro-rubric (for spot samples; 1–5, 5 = ideal):
- Coherence: does the completion follow the prompt logically? (1..5)
- Completeness: answers the full instruction / all bullets covered? (1..5)
- Hallucination: degree of invented facts (1=lots, 5=none) -> invert later if needed
- Abruptness: natural ending vs truncated/ellipsis (1=very abrupt, 5=clean end)
- Latency/Cost note: token length and avg token time observed (free-form field)

Sample probe set (short, copy to runner):
1) Prompt: "List three potential failure modes for a payment webhook integration."
   - Model v2.1.7 (control) -> "1) Duplicate events leading to idempotency issues. 2) Signature mismatch... 3) Network retries causing out-of-order delivery." (Coherence=5, Completeness=5, Hallucination=5, Abruptness=5)
   - Model v2.2.0 (suspect) -> "1) Duplicate events. 2) Signature mismatch..." (stops mid-list; Abruptness=2, Completeness=2)

2) Prompt: "Summarize the following bulleted plan for onboarding new users:\n- collect email\n- ask verification question\n- start onboarding flow"
   - v2.1.7 -> neat 3-sentence summary hitting all bullets.
   - v2.2.0 -> one short sentence, misses verification bullet.

3) Prompt: "Translate to French: 'We will ship the update on Tuesday, November 5th.'"
   - v2.1.7 -> correct translation.
   - v2.2.0 -> correct but ends with trailing ellipsis token and short stop occasionally.

Quick notes from raw logs (what to grep):
- Look for increased frequency of <eos> token emission immediately after punctuation tokens like "." "," "-" or numeric markers.
- Compare token-level probs in token window [t-3, t] across control vs suspect.
- Filter for prompts with list-like prefixes or multiple short instructions.

Sampling plan (small, actionable):
- n=200 paired prompts (control vs suspect config) drawn from: help-center articles (50), developer instructions (50), translation set (50), micro-prompts with bullets (50).
- Measure: per-sample rubric scores, average output length, frequency of stop within 3 tokens after punctuation, top-1 token entropy delta.
- Run on both quantization variants (8-bit vs 16-bit) and an isolated CPU baseline if possible.

Immediate quick checks to run now: (short term)
- Re-run 30 bullet prompts against the canary with debug token logits enabled; save deltas. (assign: Ivy)
- Pull serving runtime logs for kernel selection changes between rollouts (ask infra: Noah).
- Run tokenizer diff between v2.1.7 and v2.2.0 artifacts (me).

Longer-run checks (next week):
- Full 200-pair sweep + small analysis notebook (plot abruptness distribution).
- If kernel change implicated, run a micro-benchmark toggling the new code path.
- If quantization implicated, test lowering temp and widening top-k to see interaction surface.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Keep rubric lightweight; the goal is triage not full eval.
- If >30% of samples show abruptness drop (avg abruptness <=3), escalate to rollback ticket.
- Record any reproduction locally with exact model artifact hashes.

Observational aside: sometimes the truncated endings read like "..." because the sampling distribution spikes on a punctuation token that our token-to-text decoding maps to an EOS-like subtokens sequence. Need to confirm if this is decoding or model-level.

Why "closet" in name: quick stash of rough bits — not meant for docs yet. If we converge to a root cause, migrate cleaned findings to: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/8573-eval-runbook

End log.
